    Audit grade

    One grade, from the nine named checks and the anomaly log.

    —

    Grade not computed yet

    —

    How the grade is scored
    • A+ All 9 checks pass and the anomaly log is empty.
    • A All 9 checks pass, but anomalies were logged.
    • B 1 check fails.
    • C 2 checks fail.
    • F 3 or more checks fail, or any critical check fails: rootMatchesNotes, commitmentsUnique, soldClaimedSpent or noDupListingNullifiers. A critical failure overrides every other rule.

              How it works
              
            
              A scheduled job does the work; this page shows the result.
              
            
              Every 10 minutes. Swanix's key stays on the server and never touches this page.
              
          
              
          
              
            
              
              
              01
              Fetch
              
              
              
                
              Fetch the full public state
              
                
              A scheduled server-side job calls GET /state and GET /pieces/info with Swanix's key: roots, notes, nullifiers, mints and listings. Nothing private, no owners.
              
              
              
            
              
            
              
              
              02
              Recompute
              
              
              
                
              Recompute the SHA-256 digest independently
              
                
              The job rebuilds the digest exactly as the spec defines it and compares it with what the indexer publishes.
              
              
              
            
              
            
              
              
              03
              Scan
              
              
              
                
              Scan for duplicates and double-spends
              
                
              The same piece listed or minted twice, or a nullifier used twice, is what a forged proof would leave behind.
              
              
              
            
              
            
              
              
              04
              Publish
              
              
              
                
              Publish the result here
              
                
              The results replace the audit data on this page. Live chain status still comes straight from the keyless /status endpoint.
              
              
              
            
              
          
              
          
              
            
              Why this monitor exists
              
            
              
              The protocol docs note that the proving system's trusted setup had a single contribution. If that secret
              was ever kept, someone could forge proofs. Forgeries can't be seen directly, but they would show up as
              duplicate pieces or reused nullifiers — so this page watches for exactly that.
